scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Night of the Sanyasi: Siddavesa
This is Siddavesa. Traditional.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is rooted in the Natha Pantha tradition and is performed by the Arebhahse people of Sullia.
It is a traditional, religious folk dance that has been passed down through generations.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed during the full moon of the Suggi month.
It is a religious and traditional folk dance that involves visiting homes to perform for the community.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers gather at a holy place, then move from house to house.
They set up a lamp in the courtyard and dance around it.
The performance involves mythological mimicry, acting, singing, and dancing.
Watch for Sanyasi Roam.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Performers move in a group from house to house and dance in a circle around a central lamp.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music consists of singing and rhythmic chanting.
Instruments mentioned include the conch and the drum, which are carried by the Dasayya character.
Listen for the Conch, Drum.
The sound is defined by the loud, rhythmic chanting of 'Ḍimbisāle' as the troupe travels, followed by singing and the sound of the conch and drum during the courtyard performance.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes vary by character: the Sanyasi wears dried camouflage leaves and a symbolic wooden phallus; the Bhatru wears a white dhoti, sacred thread, and sandalwood paste; the Dasayya wears a white dhoti, red shawl, and carries a conch and drum; the Koraga uses dark body paint; the Byari wears a white banyan and a traditional hat.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is a religious and traditional folk performance involving prayers to local spirits and ancestors; outsiders should respect the ritual nature of the performance and the sanctity of the Guttu house or Daivradhane Chavadi.
